title: Sardegna Runs Just Above the National Line on Petrol and Diesel, and Metano Tells the Bigger Story
dek: Latest figures for 3 October 2026, read against the tracked weeks since late July.
executive_summary: As of 3 October 2026, the latest day in the feed, Sardegna's self-service petrol (Benzina) averaged €2.0649 per litre and self-service diesel (Gasolio) €2.2752, against national averages of €2.0636 and €2.2719. Both fell on the day, petrol by 0.51% and diesel by 0.53%, and both sit a fraction above Italy, by 0.06% and 0.15%. LPG is the outlier: at €0.8857 it is 16.7% above the national €0.7588 and did not move from the previous day. Self-service metano is not reported for the region at all; only a served price of €1.90 appears in the file.

Zoom out to the weekly series, which starts with the first tracked week in late July, and the picture shifts. Sardegna's petrol and diesel have each climbed about 6.5% since then, against national rises of about 6.2%, so the region has moved from slightly below Italy's average to slightly above it. The most interesting cross-fuel finding is metano: nationally its self-service price rose 20.6% across the same weeks, the steepest climb of the four fuels, while the regional series holds no self-service metano price in any week. The national trend is real, but this region's data cannot show it.

fuel_sections.heading: Petrol sits a hair above Italy after a long climb
paragraphs: Benzina in Sardegna closed the latest reading at €2.0649 self-service, down €0.0105 (−0.51%) from €2.0754 the day before. Italy's self-service average stood at €2.0636, so the region is 0.06% above the national figure, effectively level. The served price tells a similar story: €2.2034 locally against €2.2084 nationally, a 0.23% discount.

Over the tracked weeks the regional petrol average rose from €1.9751 in the first week (W30) to €2.1027 in W40, a gain of 6.5%. Nationally the same window moved from €1.9756 to €2.0979, up 6.2%. The regional peak came in the week starting 21 September at €2.1682, marginally above the national peak of €2.1669. The latest week fell 3.0% regionally and 3.2% nationally, so the cooling is shared rather than local, although W40 contains only five days and should be read as provisional.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel stays within half a percent of the national line
paragraphs: Gasolio in Sardegna is at €2.2752 self-service on the latest day, down €0.0121 (−0.53%) from €2.2873. Italy averaged €2.2719, which leaves the region 0.15% higher. Served diesel shows the same shape: €2.4309 locally against €2.4256 nationally, 0.22% above. Both measures fell by just over half a percent in a single day.

Across the tracked weeks regional diesel rose from €2.1742 to €2.3164, up 6.5%, while national diesel rose 6.2%, from €2.1747 to €2.3086. The regional premium over Italy has therefore widened from 0.02% below the national average in W30 to 0.34% above in W40. The weekly peak came in W39 for both (€2.3817 regional, €2.3736 national), and both fell 2.7% in the latest week. The spread is small, but its direction is clear in the weekly numbers.

fuel_sections.heading: LPG is the region's outlier, and its flat line deserves a closer look
paragraphs: GPL in Sardegna is listed at €0.8857 on the latest day, unchanged from the day before. National LPG stands at €0.7588, so the regional price sits 16.7% above Italy, a premium of about €0.13 per litre. The served price shows a similar gap: €0.8612 locally against €0.7647 nationally, or 12.6% above.

The regional weekly LPG average fell from €0.8990 in W30 to €0.8857 in W34 and has not moved since, an identical value across seven consecutive weeks. National LPG drifted down from €0.7592 to €0.7558 over the same window, a 0.4% decline. The regional premium has narrowed from 18.4% to 17.2%, but the stillness itself is the notable part. A price that holds to four decimal places for weeks often reflects a small number of reporting stations rather than a market that has stopped moving, so this series calls for caution rather than a firm conclusion.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano is the national story, and the regional file cannot tell it
paragraphs: Today's regional metano figure is a served price only: €1.90, up from €1.74 the previous day, a 9.2% jump in a single step. Nationally the served price stands at €1.8862 and the self-service price at €1.8354. With no regional self-service series, there is no like-for-like comparison, and a one-day move of this size should be treated as a single reading rather than a trend.

Nationally, self-service metano rose from €1.4999 in W30 to €1.8082 in W40, a 20.6% climb and the steepest of the four fuels over the tracked weeks. The latest weekly step was smaller, up 1.0% from €1.7898 in W39. The regional file records no self-service metano price in any of its eleven weekly rows, so Sardegna cannot be placed against the national curve on this fuel. For a reader, that gap is part of the finding: the national metano move is clear, while the regional self-service data stays silent.

network_section.heading: Station coverage: 90 percent reporting, and what the silent stations mean
paragraphs: On 3 October, 607 of Sardegna's 674 registered stations reported a price, a reporting rate of 90.1%. That is four more reporting stations than the day before (603). Nationally, 21,670 of 23,917 registered stations reported, or 90.6%, so the region sits essentially level with Italy on coverage.

The 67 silent stations in the region, roughly one in ten, mean every regional average here is built from most of the network rather than all of it. Against a national reporting rate of 90.6%, Sardegna's coverage is effectively the same as Italy's, so the regional and national comparisons are fair on coverage grounds. The thinner spots are the fuels with gaps in the regional file, metano above all, where the averages are the least firm.

methodology_section.heading: How this report is written, and why it is not a spreadsheet
paragraphs: This report is generated automatically every morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. The pipeline pulls the latest MIMIT price and station registry data, updates the national and regional series, selects the day's region through a fixed rotation over Italy's twenty regions keyed to the calendar date, computes the weekly averages, and drafts the written analysis. No one chooses the region, and no one retypes a figure.

The contrast with a manually maintained spreadsheet is the point. A spreadsheet is only as current as the last time someone remembered to paste in the new export, copy the formulas down and check the totals, and when a day is missed the gap is silent. The pipeline is self-correcting: if a day is skipped, the rotation still picks the right region from the calendar, and the next run pulls whatever data is available. Every number in this report comes from data the pipeline wrote that day, which is also what makes it checkable.

closing.heading: Explore the live dashboard
paragraphs: The live dashboard opens on Agip Eni's brand-level view by default. From there, use the scope picker to switch to Region, Province, Municipality or another Operator/Brand, and compare Sardegna with any other part of Italy on the same price series. The dashboard is at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/.

pull_quote: Nationally, self-service metano rose 20.6% across the tracked weeks, yet Sardegna's regional series holds no self-service metano price at all.
caption:
Today's spotlight is Sardegna. Its self-service petrol and diesel have each risen about 6.5% since late July, slightly faster than the national rise of about 6.2%, and both now sit a fraction above the Italian average.

The most striking number is metano. Nationally, self-service metano climbed 20.6% over the tracked weeks, the steepest rise of the four fuels, yet the regional series carries no self-service metano price at all. The national trend is real, but this region's data cannot show it.

Fuel Dashboard tracks Italian fuel prices daily from official MIMIT data and turns them into an interactive dashboard and a written report. Explore it at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

All of it runs unattended every morning: the data pull, the weekly analysis, the rotating region and the write-up. It was built with Claude Code, and it makes the case for AI tools over a manually maintained Excel sheet, which only stays current as long as someone remembers to update it.
